# Riverside Launches Riverside Agents, the First AI Production Team Built for Video

Press Release · Palo Alto CA, United States · via Riverside ·

Riverside, the AI-powered end-to-end content creation platform used by Spotify, NBC and the New York Times, today launched Riverside Agents: the first team of AI agents built specifically for video production. The agents take on the production work around a recording, from prepping the session to publishing the clips, and move it forward on their own. Riverside Agents are available today on web and mobile across all Riverside plans. [...] Producer preps the session and runs the studio: interview questions, talking points, scenes, layouts and branding, all ready to shape before recording starts.
 Editor turns a full-length recording into a finished episode. It proposes the editorial calls, like where to tighten the conversation and which moment makes the hook, and takes direction on what stays. Then it brings the edit to life with layouts, B-roll and motion graphics, and polishes the audio, captions and branding.
 Clipper finds the moments worth sharing and turns each one into a finished clip that’s ready to post.
 Marketer gets every clip live in the right places. It writes the post copy, creates thumbnails and plans where each clip should run, then posts or schedules it across social channels once approved. [...] Proactive by design. A creator can wrap a recording and step away while the crew keeps working. When they check back in, the edit, the clips and the posts are drafted and waiting for their call.
 Specialist AI built for video. Each agent runs on a proprietary model tuned for one job. It works with editing tools Riverside built for conversational video, like removing pauses and filler words. That makes the agents faster and lighter on compute, so creators can finish full episodes without hitting a usage limit.
 Creator in control. Nothing goes live without the creator’s approval. The agents prepare, suggest and queue up the work, and the creator decides what to hand off and what to keep hands-on. Over time, the agents learn the creator’s preferences and editing style.
